name: Reading

licensing.selective: No selective licensing in force yet. The council plans selective licensing of all privately rented homes in Battle ward first, then Redlands and Park wards in phases; its page says the formal designations have not yet been made.
licensing.additional: Borough-wide additional HMO licensing from 1 March 2026 to 28 February 2031, covering HMOs of three or four people and other HMOs outside the mandatory scheme.

privateRentedShare.text: 31.9% of households rent privately (Census 2021), up from 26.1% in 2011

housing: Reading has a large private rented sector, with almost a third of households renting privately in 2021. Victorian terraces close to the centre, in Redlands, Katesgrove, Oxford Road and Battle, are widely let as shared houses to students and young workers, and every HMO in the borough now needs a licence. The town centre has many new apartment blocks and office conversions near the station, while Whitley, Southcote and Tilehurst are mostly inter-war and post-war estates. Selective licensing is planned for Battle, Redlands and Park wards.
checkinTips: Shared houses in Redlands and near the university: note the HMO licence number and photograph each bedroom lock, fire doors, alarms and the shared kitchen separately.
Victorian terraces off Oxford Road and in Katesgrove: record damp at the base of walls, rear extensions and small yards and bins.
Apartment blocks and office conversions in the town centre: note fob counts, the intercom, parking and bike stores, and check windows and ventilation.
Homes near the Thames and the Kennet in Caversham and the centre: photograph any tide marks, damp low on walls and air bricks.
Post-war homes in Whitley and Southcote: photograph gardens, fences, sheds and older boilers.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Reading Borough Council's private sector housing team.
